meta.title: Top 100 Nutritionists 2026
meta.subtitle: The world's leading credentialed nutritionists and dietitians — ranked. Sports RDs, researcher-practitioners, clinical leaders, and the registered dietitians winning the internet.

scoreModel.name: Nutrition Authority Score
scoreModel.gate: One hard gate: recognized credentials — registered dietitian status or graduate-level nutrition science — plus real practice with clients, athletes, teams, or clinics. Famous but uncredentialed voices do not qualify.
scoreModel.notes: Reach is log-scaled and recomputed from researched follower counts. The five judgment factors — credibility, practice, content, impact, consistency — are calibrated across research segments so no category is scored on an easier curve. Counts marked verified were browser-checked at the listed date; the rest are approximate.

meta.disclaimer: Details are editorial estimates (2026) and the ranking is reviewed monthly. Educational and editorial — inclusion is not an endorsement, rankings measure influence and authority, and nothing here is dietary advice.

entries.name: Louise Burke
entries.who: PhD, APD; Professor and Chair in Sports Nutrition, Mary MacKillop Institute, Australian Catholic University; 30 years as Head of Sports Nutrition / Chief of Nutrition Strategy at the Australian Institute of Sport.
entries.why: Australian Olympic team dietitian across five Games (1996-2012); 350+ peer-reviewed papers, editor of the International Journal of Sport Nutrition and Exercise Metabolism; awarded the Order of Australia for her contribution to sports nutrition.
entries.reach: Academic/professional reach, not a personal-brand social presence (verified via search 2026-08)

entries.name: Megan Rossi
entries.who: RD, PhD (King's College London); founder and director of The Gut Health Clinic (London and Manchester) and research fellow at King's.
entries.why: Runs a real gut-health clinic and an active research fellowship at the same time, with published work (50+ papers) underpinning a large public-education platform.

entries.name: Tim Spector
entries.who: MD, PhD — Professor of Genetic Epidemiology at King's College London; pivoted a career in twin and microbiome research into founding ZOE.
entries.why: Turned twin-study and microbiome findings into the most-listened diet-science podcast and one of the largest personalized-nutrition programs in the world; nutrition is now his full-time research focus, which is why he clears the specialization gate.
entries.reach: IG in the mid hundreds of thousands; podcast in global nutrition charts (approx, unverified)

entries.name: Rujuta Diwekar
entries.who: Postgraduate degree in Sports Science & Nutrition (SNDT College, Mumbai, 1999) plus Sports Dietitians training at the Australian Institute of Sport; longtime nutritionist to Bollywood stars and the Indian cricket team.
entries.why: Set the template for mainstream Indian diet advice for two decades and reaches a bigger audience than almost any dietitian outside the anglosphere, without paid endorsements.

entries.name: Will Bulsiewicz
entries.who: MD; dual board-certified in internal medicine and gastroenterology; US Medical Director at ZOE personalized-nutrition platform.
entries.why: A practicing GI physician, not a self-taught influencer, whose Fiber Fueled work reset mainstream fiber and gut-health messaging at mass scale.

entries.name: Alan Aragon
entries.who: MS in Nutrition Science; founder of the Alan Aragon Research Review, one of the longest-running peer-vetted nutrition/fitness research digests, plus a history of consulting physique and combat athletes.
entries.why: Set the template for research-literate fitness nutrition writing that dozens of later newsletters copied; still active and cited after decades.
entries.reach: IG and X combined roughly 300K (estimate, unverified — WebSearch unavailable this session)

entries.name: Tim Noakes
entries.who: MD and Professor Emeritus of Exercise & Sports Science, University of Cape Town; decades of research on carbohydrate and fat metabolism in endurance athletes.
entries.why: Co-created the low-carb 'Banting' diet movement that reshaped South African eating habits, and was twice cleared of professional misconduct over his public advice.
entries.reach: Legacy reach via bestselling books (The Real Meal Revolution) and the Banting-diet movement; current social following unconfirmed (2026)
entries.warning: South Africa's health regulator (HPCSA) brought a professional-conduct case over his public low-carbohydrate infant-feeding advice in 2014; he was acquitted in 2017 and the regulator's appeal was dismissed in 2018.

entries.name: Asker Jeukendrup
entries.who: PhD; Director of Mysportscience Ltd, an independent sports-science and nutrition consultancy; 30 years as researcher, educator and practitioner, including a period leading Gatorade Sports Science Institute research.
entries.why: His carbohydrate-oxidation and multiple-transportable-carbohydrate research reshaped modern endurance fueling protocols now standard across pro cycling and running.
entries.reach: Newsletter/podcast audience, IG approx. mid-tens of thousands (verified business/role via site fetch 2026-08, reach not verified)

entries.name: Evelyn Tribole
entries.who: MS, RDN; co-creator of the Intuitive Eating framework, trainer of over 2,600 certified counselors worldwide, international speaker.
entries.why: Co-authored the book that defined an entire clinical counseling approach now certified and practiced globally.

entries.name: Rhiannon Lambert
entries.who: BSc, MSc, Registered Nutritionist (RNutr); founder of the Rhitrition clinic in London and Sunday Times bestselling author.
entries.why: The UK's highest-profile registered nutritionist, running an actual multi-practitioner clinic alongside books and two podcasts.

entries.name: Dr. Sarah Berry
entries.who: PhD, Professor of Nutritional Sciences at King's College London; lead scientist on ZOE's PREDICT studies, one of the largest personalized-nutrition research programs.
entries.why: PREDICT's scale (100,000+ participants) gives her population-level impact rare among nutrition researchers, and she communicates it directly to the public.
entries.reach: Personal following moderate, amplified by ZOE's platform (estimate, unverified — WebSearch unavailable this session)

entries.name: Renee McGregor
entries.who: Registered Dietitian (HCPC), clinical and performance nutrition specialist; dietitian for GB Olympic (2012), Paralympic (2016) and Commonwealth Games (2018) teams.
entries.why: Leading global voice on RED-S and the female athlete; bestselling author (Training Food, Fast Fuel, Orthorexia) bridging endurance performance and eating-disorder care.

entries.name: Dr. Stacy Sims
entries.who: PhD in Exercise Physiology and Nutrition Science — adjunct senior lecturer at the University of Waikato; consults with elite female athletes and teams.
entries.why: Built the female-specific sports-nutrition field largely from scratch; ROAR and Next Level rewired how women train and fuel.
entries.reach: IG in the low hundreds of thousands (approx, unverified)

entries.name: Marie Spano
entries.who: MS, RD, CSCS, CSSD; sports dietitian for the Washington Nationals and Atlanta Hawks, previously the Atlanta Braves (2017-2022, World Series champions 2021) and Atlanta Falcons.
entries.why: One of the most tenured active pro-team dietitians in the US, spanning MLB, NBA and NFL; lead author of the textbook Nutrition for Sport, Exercise and Health.

entries.name: Dr. Walter Willett
entries.who: MD, DrPH — Professor of Epidemiology and Nutrition at Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health; ran the Nurses' Health Study and co-chaired the EAT-Lancet Commission on planetary diets.
entries.why: The most-cited nutrition scientist alive; his cohort work and Healthy Eating Plate reshaped dietary guidelines worldwide.
entries.reach: Public profile modest relative to output; no notable social following (approx, unverified)

entries.name: James Collins
entries.who: SENr-registered performance nutritionist; founder of Performance Nutrition, longtime nutrition consultant to Arsenal FC and England Rugby.
entries.why: One of the most established practitioner names in elite UK football and rugby nutrition, with a multi-decade consultancy client list of pro clubs and national teams.
entries.reach: Primarily B2B/club-facing, limited public social presence (not verified live)

entries.name: Alberto Cormillot
entries.who: MD (Universidad de Buenos Aires, 1961) with postgraduate training in Geneva; specializes in nutrition and obesity treatment.
entries.why: Built Argentina's modern obesity-treatment infrastructure — clinics, self-help groups, and a foundation now active across several countries — over more than 60 years.

entries.name: Dr. David Ludwig
entries.who: MD, PhD — endocrinologist at Boston Children's Hospital/Harvard Medical School; runs an obesity-prevention clinic and developed the carbohydrate-insulin model of obesity.
entries.why: Bridges bench research and a working clinic; his insulin-carb framework reset the low-fat-vs-low-carb debate.
entries.reach: Modest public following; reach mainly via bestselling books (approx, unverified)

entries.name: Dr. Marion Nestle
entries.who: PhD, MPH — Paulette Goddard Professor Emerita of Nutrition, Food Studies and Public Health at NYU; author of Food Politics.
entries.why: Defined food-industry-influence scholarship; decades of books and her Food Politics blog still set the agenda for nutrition-policy debate.
entries.reach: Blog and book audience, moderate social following (approx, unverified)

entries.name: Nancy Clark
entries.who: MS, RD, CSSD; private sports-nutrition practice near Boston since the 1980s.
entries.why: Author of Nancy Clark's Sports Nutrition Guidebook, one of the field's most widely used reference texts across multiple editions; trained a generation of sports RDs.
entries.reach: Niche/legacy reach, no major social platform (not verified live)

entries.name: Iris Shai
entries.who: PhD in nutrition and epidemiology, RD, MPH; professor at Ben-Gurion University and Reichman University, adjunct at Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health.
entries.why: Her DIRECT and DIRECT-PLUS randomized trials reshaped the global low-carb-vs-Mediterranean-diet debate and guideline discussions, with 23,000-plus citations.
entries.reach: Academic reach: 23,000+ citations; no major public social-media following (verified 2026-08)

entries.name: Fan Zhihong
entries.who: PhD in Food Science; professor and doctoral advisor at China Agricultural University, director at the China Nutrition Society.
entries.why: China's most-followed nutrition science communicator, with a Weibo following in the millions and a role as the national science association's go-to nutrition voice.

entries.name: Dr. Stuart Phillips
entries.who: PhD, Professor of Kinesiology at McMaster University; the field's leading voice on dietary protein and muscle protein synthesis, especially in older adults.
entries.why: His body of work has directly shaped protein-intake guidance worldwide — a field-leading researcher whose findings changed practice, not just opinion.
entries.reach: Academic/public reach on X, tens of thousands (estimate, unverified — WebSearch unavailable this session)

entries.name: Susan Kleiner
entries.who: PhD, RD, FACN, CNS; consults with professional and Olympic athletes and strength/physique competitors.
entries.why: Author of Power Eating, a foundational strength-and-physique sports-nutrition text now in multiple editions, with decades of continuous elite-athlete consulting.

entries.name: Jean-Michel Cohen
entries.who: MD and PhD in nutrition (Université Paris Diderot, 1983); runs the Savoir Maigrir coaching program and clinics out of Paris.
entries.why: Forty years of French TV presence, a National Order of Merit for a food-labeling system, and a coaching program that scaled his practice to millions of dieters.
entries.warning: France's medical board (Ordre des médecins) sanctioned Cohen in 2015 for advertising and commercial-practice violations tied to his nutrition program; the penalty was reduced to a fine on appeal in 2017.

entries.name: Elyse Resch
entries.who: MS, RDN, CEDS-S; co-creator of Intuitive Eating, eating-disorder specialist with over 40 years in private practice.
entries.why: The clinical-practice half of the Intuitive Eating partnership, still seeing clients and training eating-disorder specialists.

entries.name: Vanessa Rissetto
entries.who: MS, RDN; co-founder and CEO of Culina Health, a large multi-dietitian telehealth practice, and still sees patients herself.
entries.why: Built one of the largest RD-led care practices in the US, scaling credentialed 1:1 nutrition care rather than just content.

entries.name: Susie Burrell
entries.who: Accredited Practising Dietitian; former dietitian to NRL clubs Parramatta Eels and St George Illawarra Dragons, now a remote-consulting dietitian.
entries.why: Twelve years as Sunrise's resident dietitian plus a podcast with 3M+ downloads make her one of Australia's most established mainstream nutrition voices.

entries.name: Graeme Close
entries.who: PhD; Professor of Human Physiology, Liverpool John Moores University; nutrition consultant to England Rugby and the PGA European Tour.
entries.why: Bridges academic research on vitamin D, protein and player welfare with hands-on consultancy for elite rugby and golf, frequently cited in UK sports-science media.
entries.reach: Academic/media reach, not a personal social brand (not verified live)

entries.name: Kate Scarlata
entries.who: MPH, RDN; Boston-based digestive-health dietitian specializing in IBS, SIBO and low-FODMAP care; co-author of The Complete Low-FODMAP Diet.
entries.why: The clinical dietitian most associated with bringing the Monash low-FODMAP research into mainstream IBS care, with 30+ years in digestive-health practice.

entries.name: Dr. Bill Campbell
entries.who: PhD; directs the Performance & Physique Enhancement Laboratory at the University of South Florida, running real studies on contest-prep and body recomposition with physique athletes.
entries.why: Bridges academic research and practice directly — his lab's contest-prep studies are widely cited across bodybuilding and physique-sport nutrition.
entries.reach: Combined social roughly 200-300K (estimate, unverified — WebSearch unavailable this session)

entries.name: Carlos Ríos
entries.who: Degree in Human Nutrition & Dietetics (Universidad Pablo de Olavide, Seville); registered dietista-nutricionista; founder of the Realfooding movement and MyRealFood app.
entries.why: Built the biggest food-literacy movement in the Spanish-speaking world, a 4.5M-strong community, even as peer dietitians criticize its traffic-light simplifications.

entries.name: Aitor Sánchez García
entries.who: Dietista-Nutricionista and food technologist (Universidad de Alicante, with honors; Universidad de Granada); doctoral researcher who has worked at Sweden's Karolinska Institutet.
entries.why: Runs both a clinical practice and 'Mi Dieta Cojea,' one of the most cited evidence-based nutrition outlets in the Spanish-speaking world.

entries.name: Leslie Bonci
entries.who: MPH, RDN, CSSD, LDN; sports-nutrition consultant, past dietitian for the Pittsburgh Steelers and Kansas City Chiefs, current consultant to Carnegie Mellon athletics and Pittsburgh Ballet Theatre.
entries.why: One of the longest-serving, most credentialed pro-team sports dietitians in the US, still actively consulting for elite teams and performing-arts companies decades in.

entries.name: Dr. Federica Amati
entries.who: Registered Nutritionist (ANutr) with a PhD — Head Nutritionist at ZOE and Clinical Lead for Nutrition at Imperial College Health Partners.
entries.why: Translates population science into daily clinical and consumer guidance at scale; author of a bestselling nutrition-myth book.
entries.reach: IG in the low hundreds of thousands (approx, unverified)

entries.name: Abbey Sharp
entries.who: Registered Dietitian (Toronto), runs Abbey's Kitchen media brand, host of the Bite Back podcast.
entries.why: One of the longest-running, highest-production RD channels online; myth-busting videos and a bestselling book give her outsized field visibility.
entries.reach: IG 426K (verified 2026-08); also active on YouTube and TikTok

entries.name: Dr. Valter Longo
entries.who: PhD in Biochemistry — Professor of Gerontology and Biological Sciences at USC and Director of the USC Longevity Institute; developed the Fasting-Mimicking Diet.
entries.why: Turned lab longevity research into a clinically tested dietary intervention now used in hospitals and licensed commercially.
entries.reach: Moderate public following, larger in Italy/Europe (approx, unverified)

entries.name: Christy Harrison
entries.who: Registered Dietitian, MPH, Certified Eating Disorders Specialist (CEDS); journalist turned intuitive-eating coach and author.
entries.why: Her book Anti-Diet is widely cited as a movement-defining text; long-running Food Psych / Rethinking Wellness podcasts shaped anti-diet nutrition media.
entries.reach: Podcast + Substack audience in the tens of thousands (approx, unverified 2026-08)

entries.name: Jose Antonio
entries.who: PhD; co-founder and CEO of the International Society of Sports Nutrition (ISSN), professor at Nova Southeastern University.
entries.why: Runs the field's leading professional/research society and its position stands on protein and supplementation, shaping how sports-nutrition guidelines are written and cited worldwide.

entries.name: Martin MacDonald
entries.who: SENr-registered nutritionist running Mac-Nutrition Uni and a clinical practice that has worked with British elite athletics and rugby programs.
entries.why: One of the few names on this list whose day job is fueling actual elite teams, not just talking about it online.
entries.reach: Moderate UK following, tens of thousands (estimate, unverified — WebSearch unavailable this session)

entries.name: Dr. Spencer Nadolsky
entries.who: DO, board-certified in obesity medicine and lipidology; treats patients directly on weight and metabolic health and co-hosts the Docs Who Lift podcast.
entries.why: A working physician-nutrition voice in the increasingly loud GLP-1/obesity-medicine conversation, grounded in an active clinical practice.
entries.reach: Combined social roughly 150K+ (estimate, unverified — WebSearch unavailable this session)

entries.name: Brenda Davis
entries.who: RD; plant-based nutrition specialist and author who has led diabetes-nutrition programs with the Pima Nation and in the Marshall Islands.
entries.why: Among the most credentialed, longest-standing plant-based dietitians, with population-level clinical program results behind the books.

entries.name: Dr. Idrees Mughal (Dr. Idz)
entries.who: MBBS plus an MRes in nutrition research; UK-trained physician who debunks carnivore, vegan-extremist, and fad-diet claims at scale on YouTube, TikTok, and Instagram.
entries.why: Among the highest-reach myth-busting voices in the space, using a genuine research background to fact-check viral diet claims in near-real time.
entries.reach: TikTok/IG combined likely well over 1M (estimate, unverified — WebSearch unavailable this session)

entries.name: Dr. Eric Trexler
entries.who: PhD in Human Movement Science; Director of Research at MASS (Monthly Applied Science in Sport), a peer-reviewed-literature digest for coaches and dietitians.
entries.why: MASS is treated as a reference standard by strength/physique coaches for staying current on primary research without wading through journals themselves.
entries.reach: Combined social roughly 150-250K (estimate, unverified — WebSearch unavailable this session)

entries.name: Dr. Christopher Gardner
entries.who: PhD — Director of Nutrition Studies at the Stanford Prevention Research Center; led the landmark DIETFITS low-fat vs. low-carb trial.
entries.why: Runs some of the most rigorous, most-cited diet-comparison trials in the field.
entries.reach: Academic reach with occasional mainstream press, no verified following (approx, unverified)

entries.name: Trent Stellingwerff
entries.who: PhD; sport physiologist/nutrition lead at the Canadian Sport Institute Pacific, supporting Team Canada Olympic and world-championship athletes.
entries.why: Applied "mission nutrition" performance frameworks used across Canadian high-performance sport; active researcher-practitioner bridging lab science and Games-time fueling.

entries.name: Julio Basulto
entries.who: Registered dietitian-nutritionist (colegiado CAT000943, Barcelona); editor of the Spanish Journal of Human Nutrition and Dietetics.
entries.why: Decades of clinical practice paired with prolific myth-debunking books and talks that have shaped Spain's public nutrition debate.

entries.name: Dr. Frank Hu
entries.who: MD, PhD — Chair of the Department of Nutrition at Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health; leads large-scale cohort research on diet, diabetes and cardiovascular risk.
entries.why: One of the most-published nutrition epidemiologists in the world; his work underpins global diabetes-prevention guidance.
entries.reach: Academic profile, no notable public social following (approx, unverified)

entries.name: Dr. Michael Greger
entries.who: MD — founder of NutritionFacts.org, the largest free video library of evidence reviews on nutrition; author of How Not to Die.
entries.why: Borderline on current clinical practice, but the scale and rigor of his evidence-synthesis library is field-defining for plant-based nutrition education.
entries.reach: Video and newsletter audience in the high hundreds of thousands to low millions (approx, unverified)

entries.name: Dawn Jackson Blatner
entries.who: RDN, CSSD; former Chicago Cubs team dietitian, now a private-practice dietitian and regular Today Show/GMA nutrition contributor.
entries.why: Two-decade media career plus an elite-sports practice history; her Flexitarian Diet book shaped mainstream plant-forward eating advice.

entries.name: Keri Glassman
entries.who: Registered Dietitian, founder of the Nutritious Life brand and a coach-certification program that trains other nutrition professionals.
entries.why: Built a practice-plus-media-plus-training brand model that predates and influenced today's dietitian-influencer business playbook.

entries.name: Cynthia Sass
entries.who: MPH, MA, RD, CSSD; performance dietitian who has consulted for the New York Yankees and other pro athletes; longtime Health magazine contributing nutrition editor.
entries.why: A rare RD with genuine pro-sports clinical credentials paired with a two-decade national media platform.

entries.name: Jennifer Anderson
entries.who: RD, MS in public health (Johns Hopkins); founder of Kids Eat in Color and CEO of BetterBites, digital feeding-therapy programs for families.
entries.why: Runs an actual clinical treatment platform for picky eating and feeding challenges while building one of the largest pediatric-feeding audiences among credentialed dietitians.

entries.name: Dan Benardot
entries.who: PhD, RD; professor emeritus, Georgia State University; nutrition consultant to US Olympic gymnastics and figure-skating programs.
entries.why: Academic authority on energy availability and micro-periodized eating for aesthetic/weight-sensitive sports, author of the textbook Advanced Sports Nutrition.
entries.reach: Academic reach, no notable social platform (not verified live)

entries.name: Jill Castle
entries.who: MS, RDN; pediatric dietitian in private practice (Jill Castle Nutrition), author of six children's-nutrition books, host of The Nourished Child podcast.
entries.why: Over 30 years translating hands-on pediatric feeding-practice work into parent-facing guidance and clinical training.

entries.name: Maya Feller
entries.who: Maya Feller, MS, RD, CDN; runs a Brooklyn private practice and is a regular nutrition expert on Good Morning America.
entries.why: Combines an active clinical practice with mainstream broadcast reach and a culturally-rooted nutrition book, a rare full-stack profile.

entries.name: Lyndi Cohen
entries.who: Accredited Practising Dietitian (APD) and Accredited Nutritionist; "The Nude Nutritionist," TV nutritionist on Australia's Today Show.
entries.why: Leading Australian anti-diet dietitian voice with a TEDx talk, podcast, and coaching programs reaching a large binge-eating-recovery audience.

entries.name: Bonnie Taub-Dix
entries.who: RDN, CDN; founder of BTD Nutrition Consultants and author of Read It Before You Eat It; longtime national media spokesperson for the Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics.
entries.why: Three-decade mainstream media career built consumer nutrition-label literacy at national scale, ahead of the current creator wave.

entries.name: Meghann Featherstun
entries.who: RD, CSSD, known as "The Marathon Nutritionist"; runs a private practice and online coaching for runners at Featherstun Nutrition.
entries.why: Built one of the largest audiences in run-specific fueling education, translating clinical sports-nutrition guidance into practical marathon and half-marathon fueling content.
entries.reach: IG approx. 400-600K (handle confirmed live 2026-08, follower count not verified)

entries.name: Antonio Paoli
entries.who: MD and Full Professor of Exercise & Sport Sciences, University of Padova; directs its Nutrition & Exercise Physiology Laboratory, with a second professorship at UCAM Murcia, Spain.
entries.why: One of the most-cited researchers on ketogenic diets and athletic performance, with a body of work widely applied in sports-nutrition practice.
entries.reach: Academic reach: ~21K citations, h-index 48; minimal public social-media following (verified 2026-08)

entries.name: Dr. Nicola Guess
entries.who: Registered Dietitian and PhD, University of Oxford; researches low-carbohydrate diets and type 2 diabetes remission, with direct clinical work on diabetes nutrition.
entries.why: Respected voice bridging clinical dietetics and diabetes research, known for pushing back on both low-carb hype and knee-jerk dismissals of it.
entries.reach: Modest academic/public following, low tens of thousands (estimate, unverified — WebSearch unavailable this session)

entries.name: Wendy Lopez & Jessica Jones
entries.who: Two Registered Dietitians who co-host the long-running Food Heaven Made Easy podcast and brand.
entries.why: Early, decade-plus voices in diet-culture-critical, culturally inclusive nutrition media; influenced the current wave of anti-diet RD podcasters.
entries.reach: IG approx. 140K, podcast running 10+ years (approx, unverified 2026-08)

entries.name: Chris Rosenbloom
entries.who: PhD, RDN, CSSD; professor emerita, Georgia State University; nutrition consultant to the Atlanta Ballet and collegiate athletes.
entries.why: Widely cited sports-nutrition textbook co-author and educator who helped formalize sports RD training programs in the US.
entries.reach: Academic reach, no notable social platform (not verified live)

entries.name: Dr. Kevin Klatt
entries.who: PhD in Nutritional Sciences (Cornell), postdoctoral researcher at UC Berkeley, and Director of Research at Examine.com.
entries.why: Deep technical rigor on micronutrient and supplement science, shaping how thousands of practitioners interpret primary literature via Examine.
entries.reach: Niche academic/practitioner following on X, tens of thousands (estimate, unverified — WebSearch unavailable this session)

entries.name: Bob Seebohar
entries.who: MS, RD, CSSD, CSCS; sports dietitian for USA Triathlon across multiple Olympic cycles, founder of Fuel4mance.
entries.why: Longtime Olympic-team practitioner known for periodized/metabolic-efficiency fueling approaches adopted across endurance coaching.

entries.name: Pooja Makhija
entries.who: BSc in Dietetics and MSc in Food Science & Nutrition; clinical nutritionist running a Mumbai practice for Bollywood clients and metabolic-health patients.
entries.why: One of India's most visible clinical nutritionists, with an ongoing consulting practice and a bestselling book that shaped celebrity-diet coverage.

entries.name: Danny Lennon
entries.who: MSc in Nutrition & Sports Performance; founder of Sigma Nutrition, a long-running evidence-based podcast and CPD education company for nutrition professionals.
entries.why: One of the most consistently rigorous interview-format nutrition podcasts, widely used by dietitians and coaches for continuing education.
entries.reach: Niche podcast audience, low tens of thousands (estimate, unverified — WebSearch unavailable this session)

entries.name: Dr. Susie Burrell
entries.who: Accredited Practising Dietitian (APD); runs a private clinic and hosts the Shared Plate podcast, a prominent Australian nutrition-myth-busting voice.
entries.why: Leading credentialed nutrition voice in the Australian market, with a practice and media footprint that has lasted well over a decade.
entries.reach: Moderate, likely low hundreds of thousands combined (estimate, unverified — WebSearch unavailable this session)

entries.name: Steph Grasso
entries.who: Registered Dietitian, clinically trained, now a full-time TikTok/Instagram recipe-and-nutrition-education creator.
entries.why: One of the highest-reach RDs on TikTok, credited with popularizing the fast, credentialed grocery-haul/recipe format many other dietitians now copy.

entries.name: Rebecca Gawthorne
entries.who: Accredited Practising Dietitian, founder of the Nourish Naturally brand.
entries.why: One of the largest Instagram followings of any credentialed dietitian worldwide, built on consistent non-diet, family-nutrition content.

entries.name: Amy Goodson
entries.who: MS, RD, CSSD; sports dietitian for the Dallas Cowboys and multiple pro and college athletic programs.
entries.why: One of the more visible NFL team dietitians in US sports media, regularly quoted on pro-athlete fueling and recovery nutrition.

entries.name: Frédéric Saldmann
entries.who: MD, dual-trained as a cardiologist and nutritionist, practicing out of Paris hospitals.
entries.why: One of France's most consistent bestselling health authors, translating preventive-medicine research into mass-market nutrition advice for two decades.
entries.reach: Multiple bestselling books; exact current social-media following unconfirmed (2026)

entries.name: Dr. Gabrielle Fundaro
entries.who: PhD in Human Nutrition, Foods, and Exercise; coaches clients on gut health and behavior change through an evidence-based physique coaching group.
entries.why: Rare combination of gut-health research depth and applied behavior-change coaching, filling a gap most fitness-nutrition educators skip.
entries.reach: Moderate niche following, tens of thousands (estimate, unverified — WebSearch unavailable this session)

entries.name: Abby Langer
entries.who: Registered Dietitian, private practice in Toronto and long-time nutrition writer for outlets like Self and Glamour.
entries.why: Known for plain-spoken, myth-debunking commentary that pushes back on wellness-industry overreach from inside the profession.

entries.name: Stephanie Howe
entries.who: PhD in Nutrition and Exercise Physiology, RD; former elite ultrarunner (Western States 100 champion) now consulting with endurance athletes.
entries.why: Rare combination of doctoral research training, RD credential and elite athletic pedigree, giving her fueling guidance unusual credibility in the ultra-endurance space.

entries.name: Frederico Lobo
entries.who: MD with a registered nutrology specialization (CRM-GO 13192, RQE 11915), certified by ABRAN; practices in Goiânia, Brazil.
entries.why: Helped found the Movimento Nutrologia Brasil in 2014 and built one of Brazil's most-watched physician-led nutrition YouTube channels.
entries.reach: YouTube channel + Brazilian media presence; current subscriber count unconfirmed (2026)

entries.name: Emily Leeming
entries.who: RD, PhD; nutrition scientist at King's College London, author of Genius Gut (2024).
entries.why: Translates King's/ZOE gut-microbiome cohort research into clinical dietetic guidance, a newer but credentialed voice in the gut-health space.

entries.name: Dr. Adrian Chavez
entries.who: PhD in Nutritional Sciences; runs a private nutrition coaching practice and hosts a long-running evidence-based nutrition podcast.
entries.why: Steady, credentialed voice translating primary research for both clients and a lay audience without the hype common in the space.
entries.reach: Modest, tens of thousands (estimate, unverified — WebSearch unavailable this session)

entries.name: Dr. Duane Mellor
entries.who: Registered Dietitian and PhD, senior lecturer at Aston University; regular British Dietetic Association spokesperson on fad diets and nutrition myths in UK media.
entries.why: The go-to credentialed rebuttal voice in British press and broadcast whenever a new diet trend or misinformation claim goes viral.
entries.reach: Modest social following; reach is mostly via traditional media, not counted here (estimate, unverified — WebSearch unavailable this session)

entries.name: Dr. Gil Carvalho
entries.who: MD, PhD (biophysics) — physician-scientist behind Nutrition Made Simple!, an evidence-review channel fact-checking nutrition claims.
entries.why: One of the few MDs doing rigorous, citation-backed myth-busting at real scale; borderline on active clinical practice, but the education work is genuinely field-shaping.
entries.reach: Subscriber base in the low hundreds of thousands (approx, unverified)

entries.name: Prof. Susan Jebb
entries.who: PhD — Professor of Diet and Population Health at the University of Oxford and Chair of the UK Food Standards Agency.
entries.why: Shapes UK national nutrition and food-safety policy directly; decades advising government on obesity and diet.
entries.reach: Academic/policy profile, minimal public social presence (approx, unverified)

entries.name: Yasi Ansari
entries.who: MS, RDN, CSSD; sports dietitian for UCLA Athletics and national media spokesperson for the Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics.
entries.why: Practices with Division I athletes while serving as the profession's own national voice in mainstream media.

entries.name: Vesanto Melina
entries.who: RD; co-author with Brenda Davis of foundational plant-based nutrition texts (Becoming Vegan, Becoming Raw) and a longtime plant-based dietetics educator.
entries.why: Co-wrote reference texts that clinical plant-based dietetic practice still draws on today.

entries.name: Dr. Kevin Hall
entries.who: PhD (physics) — spent two decades as a senior investigator in NIH's metabolism and nutrition research group; retired from NIH in 2025 following a public dispute over research independence; current institutional role not independently confirmed here.
entries.why: His controlled-feeding trials gave the first causal evidence that ultra-processed food drives overeating — the single most field-shifting nutrition experiment of the decade.
entries.reach: Academic and media profile, no verified social following (approx, unverified)

entries.name: Dr. Alan Flanagan
entries.who: PhD in Nutritional Sciences (University of Surrey) — Registered Associate Nutritionist running the Alinea Nutrition consultancy, specializing in circadian nutrition.
entries.why: Rare combination of a rigorous PhD and an active client-facing practice; a leading voice against nutrition-influencer overreach.
entries.reach: Modest following, mostly a professional/industry audience (approx, unverified)

entries.name: Prof. Barbara Rolls
entries.who: PhD — Helen A. Guthrie Chair of Nutritional Sciences at Penn State; created the Volumetrics approach to satiety and portion research.
entries.why: Her food-volume/energy-density research reshaped how dietitians and the public think about fullness and portion control.
entries.reach: Academic and book audience only (approx, unverified)

entries.name: Alan McCubbin
entries.who: PhD; senior lecturer at Monash University and Sports Dietitians Australia member, consulting with elite triathletes and endurance athletes.
entries.why: Active gut-training and carbohydrate-fueling researcher whose work informs current endurance-nutrition practice guidelines in Australia and beyond.

entries.name: Kylie Sakaida
entries.who: Registered Dietitian and NYT-bestselling cookbook author behind the nutritionbykylie brand.
entries.why: Among the largest personal-following RDs on Instagram; cookbook and recipe content sets a reference bar for RD-led food media.

entries.name: Niko Rittenau
entries.who: Bachelor's in nutrition counseling (DHfPG) and Master's in micronutrient therapy & regulation medicine (FHM Bielefeld); often billed as a 'nutritional scientist,' a label German media has called a stretch given his actual training.
entries.why: Set the format for plant-based nutrition education in German-speaking Europe with a Spiegel-bestselling book, though he also runs a supplement business — a disclosed conflict of interest worth flagging.

entries.name: Kelly Jones
entries.who: RD, CSSD; sports dietitian in private practice (Student Athlete Nutrition), regular contributor to Runner's World and other outlets.
entries.why: Working clinical sports dietitian whose one-on-one athlete practice feeds a long-running national nutrition-journalism byline.

entries.name: Toby Smithson
entries.who: MS, RDN, CDCES; diabetes lifestyle specialist, founder of DiabetesEveryDay, author of Diabetes Meal Planning and Nutrition for Dummies.
entries.why: One of the most established diabetes-specialist dietitians, bridging one-on-one CDCES clinical counseling with widely used patient education.

entries.name: Nichole Andrews
entries.who: Registered Dietitian specializing in oncology nutrition, working directly with cancer patients as the "Dietitian Cancer Coach."
entries.why: Fills a genuine clinical-education gap: credentialed, practice-based guidance for cancer patients navigating nutrition myths during treatment.

entries.name: Prof. Jose Ordovas
entries.who: PhD — Director of the Nutrition and Genomics Laboratory at Tufts University's Jean Mayer USDA Human Nutrition Research Center.
entries.why: Founding figure of nutrigenomics; his gene-diet interaction studies (e.g., Mediterranean-diet research) underlie the whole personalized-nutrition field.

entries.name: Angie Asche
entries.who: RD, CSSD; founder of Eleat Sports Nutrition, working with collegiate and endurance athletes, author of Chase the Podium.
entries.why: Runs a visible independent sports-dietitian practice and extends its clinical fueling work into published athlete-nutrition education.

entries.name: Kelly Pritchett
entries.who: PhD, RD, CSSD; sports-nutrition professor at Central Washington University and team dietitian consultant.
entries.why: Combines an academic research role with hands-on team consulting, representative of the researcher-practitioner track in sports dietetics.

entries.name: Dr. Gemma Newman
entries.who: MBBS — practicing NHS GP in the UK ('The Plant Power Doctor') focused on lifestyle and plant-based nutrition in primary care.
entries.why: Borderline on formal nutrition-science credentials, but an active GP practice plus consistent, credentialed public education on diet and chronic disease.
entries.reach: IG in the tens to low hundreds of thousands (approx, unverified)

entries.name: Kylee Van Horn
entries.who: RD specializing in trail and ultrarunning nutrition; works one-on-one with professional trail and ultra athletes.
entries.why: One of the few dietitians with a dedicated ultra-endurance/trail-running client base, filling a gap most sports-nutrition figures don't cover.

entries.name: Sarah Remmer
entries.who: RD; Alberta-based pediatric and prenatal dietitian in private practice, author and parenting-nutrition writer.
entries.why: A leading Canadian clinical voice on infant, toddler and prenatal feeding, working one-on-one with families alongside her writing.

entries.name: Dr. Sumantra Ray
entries.who: Physician-scientist — founder and Chair of the NNEdPro Global Institute for Food, Nutrition and Health, a WHO-collaborating nutrition-education program spanning over 100 countries.
entries.why: Built the largest cross-border nutrition-in-medicine education network, training clinicians worldwide to actually use nutrition science.
entries.reach: Institutional/academic reach, no personal social following (approx, unverified)

entries.name: Colleen Christensen
entries.who: Registered Dietitian behind the No Food Rules brand, focused on flexible, non-restrictive eating content.
entries.why: Consistent, high-volume recipe and mindset content with a large, engaged following among mainstream (non-diet) nutrition audiences.

bubblingUnder.name: Alex Larson
bubblingUnder.who: RD, CSSD; founder of Fuel2Run, a practice coaching endurance runners on fueling and RED-S prevention.
bubblingUnder.why: Consistent, practical endurance-runner-focused education and coaching, filling the day-to-day fueling advice gap for recreational-to-competitive runners.

bubblingUnder.name: Shyla Cadogan
bubblingUnder.who: Registered Dietitian based in Washington, DC, with a private practice and frequent contributor role for national health outlets.
bubblingUnder.why: Steady media-dietitian output translating clinical nutrition into consumer-press guidance.
